text:
Dallas won the first period on chances and had nothing to show for it beyond a late power-play goal. The Stars out-chanced Colorado 1.37 to 0.64 in expected goals, and Sam Steel had the best look of the night, a 27% chance that missed the net. Artturi Lehkonen scored on a backhand at 11:32 from a 14% chance, and Tyler Seguin tied it at 19:06 on the power play.

The game turned in the second, when Colorado took over the chances, 1.27 to 0.92. Martin Necas scored at 3:05 on a slap shot and again at 16:14 on the power play, a 20% chance, to make it 3-1. Necas was on the ice for 1.38 expected goals for and 0.27 against, and Nathan MacKinnon, who assisted on the first, was at 1.78 and 0.25. Colorado played even strength to a 1.84 to 2.17 deficit but won on special teams, with 1.07 expected goals on its three power plays.

Roope Hintz cut it to 3-2 at 3:17 of the third, but Dallas had little more. Colorado held the period 1.40 to 0.34 in expected goals, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 24 of 26 shots, 0.63 goals better than expected. Dallas took 59 shot attempts to Colorado's 47 and won 36 of 56 faceoffs, yet the simulations give the Stars only a 45% share of deserved wins. Jake Oettinger allowed three on 25 shots, close to the 2.9 expected.
